newsitem.title: USA: U.S., UK aviation talks to go into third day.
newsitem.headline: U.S., UK aviation talks to go into third day.

text.p: U.S. and British aviation negotiators met on Wednesday for a second day to try to fashion a free-market aviation agreement, and will meet again on Thursday, a State Department official said.
He said he could not report on whether any progress was being made in the talks, which have been been held on and off for the past two years, but said a third day had been scheduled.

The United States wants to end the current restrictive U.S.-British aviation services agreement and replace it with an "open skies" pact that woud give airlines greater freedom to fly routes and frequencies of their own choosing.
Past talks have been held up by Britain's reluctance to allow additional U.S. flights to London's Heathrow airport, which is dominated by British Airways Plc.
Heathrow is considered a key transfer point for travel beyond Britain to continental Europe.
